stories.title: TikTok to pay $400 million in DOJ child privacy settlement
stories.summary: TikTok agreed to pay $400 million to settle a Justice Department lawsuit over children's privacy. The DOJ had accused TikTok of violating child privacy protections. The deal closes one of TikTok's biggest US legal fights.
stories.whyItMatters: The payout shows regulators will extract large penalties from platforms over child safety, and it adds to TikTok's mounting US legal costs.
whatToWatch: Whether TikTok must change its data or safety practices for minors
Any new child-safety actions against other platforms
questions: What specific practices triggered the DOJ lawsuit?
Does the settlement include ongoing compliance monitoring?

stories.title: AI accounting startup Rillet raises $100M, hits unicorn status in 48 hours

stories.whyItMatters: The speed and size of the round show strong investor demand for AI tools aimed at back-office finance work.

stories.title: Over 1 million people have clicked LinkedIn's AI-content flag button
stories.summary: LinkedIn says more than 1 million people have clicked a button meant to flag AI-generated posts, often called an 'AI slop' button. The company cites the number as proof the feature gets used. It is part of a broader push by platforms to address low-quality AI content in feeds.
stories.whyItMatters: It shows how much AI-generated content now fills major platforms, and how those platforms are testing tools to let users push back.

questions: What does LinkedIn do with a post after it gets flagged?

stories.title: Apple cuts hundreds of jobs from Siri and Vision Pro teams
stories.summary: Apple is reportedly laying off hundreds of employees who worked on Siri and the Vision Pro. The cuts hit two of Apple's more troubled recent efforts: its voice assistant and its mixed-reality headset. Apple has not given a public reason beyond the reports.
stories.whyItMatters: The layoffs suggest Apple is scaling back two high-profile bets, while it faces pressure to catch up on AI and prove out Vision Pro.

stories.title: Tesla recalls millions of cars in China over hidden door handles
stories.summary: Tesla is recalling around 3 million cars in China as part of a wider industry push to fix hidden door handles. Combined with other automakers, reports put the total recall at more than 4 million vehicles. Regulators are targeting handle designs that can trap occupants or block first responders after a crash.
stories.whyItMatters: Hidden door handles have become a safety flashpoint across the EV industry, and a recall this size could push automakers worldwide to rethink the design.
whatToWatch: Whether other markets adopt China's hidden-handle rules
How Tesla implements the fix, hardware swap or software update
questions: Is the fix a physical replacement or a redesign?
Which other automakers are included in the recall?

stories.title: Nvidia's demo suggests the 'harness' matters more than the AI model itself
stories.summary: A TechCrunch analysis argues Nvidia's latest demonstration shows the system around an AI model, its 'harness,' now matters more than the model itself. The piece frames this as a shift in where AI performance gains come from. It points to Nvidia's role in building that surrounding infrastructure and tooling.
stories.whyItMatters: If the harness around a model drives more real-world performance than the model itself, competitive advantage in AI shifts toward infrastructure providers like Nvidia.
whatToWatch: Whether other AI infrastructure providers make similar claims
How model makers respond to this framing
questions: What exactly did Nvidia demonstrate?
